newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 7.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 7. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto said Indonesia will continue to develop the agricultural sector even though it plans to become an industrial country.

Two minority parties, the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said they were running out of money to participate in the May 29 general elections. The government grants fund for the the three political parties contesting in the elections. The ruling Golkar party is known to have abundant financial and human resources.

Sacked Indonesian legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas has been charged with subversion, which carries a maximum penalty of death, for sending festive cards urging people to boycott the May 29 general elections.
President Suharto said there are groups of people who wish to see the country disintegrate. He said the government will take stern action against people who attempt to create disunity in the country.
